title: Propolis collection and uses
subtitle: How bees make it, how to collect it, and what to do with it.
excerpt: Propolis is a resinous material bees collect from tree buds and use to seal gaps and coat the inside of the hive. It is antifungal and antibacterial. Beekeepers can collect propolis using a propolis trap, freeze it, and use it in homemade salves and skin preparations.
sourceNotes: BBKA factsheet on hive products and propolis. NBU Beekeeper's Toolkit (2024). British Bee Vets Association, Hive Products guidance.

glossaryTerms.definition: A resinous mixture collected by honeybees from tree buds, sap, and plant wounds. Used in the hive to seal small gaps, coat the entrance, and cover foreign bodies the bees cannot remove.

content.text: by blending plant resins with wax and saliva. It is sticky at hive temperature (around 35°C), hard and brittle below 15°C, and its composition varies with the tree species available. Beekeepers who work with dark propolis from birch and poplar areas end up with a stronger, darker product than those near conifers.

A propolis trap is a sheet of plastic or rubber with a grid of narrow slots, placed where the crown board usually sits. The bees seal the slots with propolis. Collection takes four to six weeks in summer.
Lay the propolis trap flat across the top of the frames, in place of the crown board. The roof sits directly on the trap.
Leave the trap in place for four to six weeks through July and August, when propolis production is at its peak.
Remove the trap on a cool morning (below 15°C if possible, or chill it in the freezer for an hour beforehand). The propolis becomes brittle when cold and snaps cleanly from the trap.
Flex the trap sharply over a clean tray or sheet of paper. The propolis fragments fall out. Collect them into a sealed bag and freeze for at least 24 hours before use.
What to do with raw propolis

Propolis extract: dissolve 10 g of frozen, powdered propolis in 100 ml of high-proof vodka or grain alcohol. Shake daily for two weeks, then strain through muslin. The amber extract can be applied neat to small skin cuts or stirred into lip balm.
Propolis salve: melt 100 ml beeswax into 200 ml coconut oil over a bain-marie, stir in 5 ml propolis extract off the heat, pour into tins. Use on dry or cracked skin.
Hive coating: dissolve raw propolis in a little alcohol and brush it onto the inside of a new wooden hive box. This mimics the bees' own lining and may help the colony settle in more quickly.

attrs.title: Removing propolis from tools and clothing

content.text: Propolis stains are nearly permanent on fabric. Freeze the garment first, scrape off the brittle propolis, then treat the remaining stain with rubbing alcohol or surgical spirit before washing. Hive tools should be cleaned while propolis is warm and workable, using a scraper, not a cloth.
